players.note: Will Anderson stayed hot in Week 9, racking up two solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Anderson leads the league with 9.5 sacks, keeping him locked in as a weekly top-three option regardless of opponent. Treat him as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Myles Garrett returned with a bang in Week 9, racking up three solos, three sacks, three tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Garrett delivered and then overdelivered in his first game as a Ram and is obviously locked back in as a top-five option going forward.

David Bailey stayed hot in Week 9, racking up five solos, four assists, two sacks, three tackles for loss, and two forced fumbles. The DL1 overall and in fppg, Bailey is up to 7.5 sacks on the season. Count the Jets edge rusher as a top-five play for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Greg Rousseau was back at it in Week 9, reeling off one solo, one sack, one tackle for loss, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended. The Bills edge rusher is up to eight sacks on the season, with a sack in each of his last two games. Fire Rousseau up as a top-10 option for a tasty Week 10 matchup against the New York Jets.

Andrew Van Ginkel was at it again in Week 9, racking up two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. AVG is up to 7.5 sacks on the season, with 3.5 of them coming in his last two games. The DL10 in fppg, Van Ginkel is a top-15 play whenever he is in the midst of a hot streak. Count him as just that for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Carl Granderson stayed hot in Week 9, tallying five solos, two assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Granderson has been on fire for the Saints and is now up to 7.5 sacks on the season, with at least 1.5 sacks in an incredible four straight games. Granderson needs to be treated as a top-15 play until he cools down. Act accordingly ahead of a plus Week 10 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Arvell Reese went off in Week 9, exploding with 10 solos, two assists, three sacks, three tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Reese proved he can have an early-career Micah Parsons like impact, logging three sacks, with just one coming off the edge. Reese is up to 4.5 sacks on the season and has pushed his way to LB1 in fppg after nine weeks of action. Count Reese as a top-five play at the position going forward.

Dallas Turner was excellent in Week 9, racking up two solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Ninth in the league with 7.0 sacks, Turner is locked in as a top-12 DL option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

T.J. Watt was back at it in Week 8, reeling off two solos, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. T.J. is up to 7.5 sacks on the season, with three of them coming in his last two games. The DL5 in fppg heading into the Steelers' Week 9 bye, treat Watt as an easy top-five option for a tasty Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

George Karlaftis was back at it in Week 9, tallying four solos, two assists, two sacks, three tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Furious George is now up to four sacks on the season, with all four coming in three of his last four games. Count the Chiefs edge rusher as a top-20 option for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Chase Young stayed hot in Week 9, racking up two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Chase is second in the league with eight sacks, with at least one in three straight games. With that said, Young has provided limited production outside of the sacks, keeping him out of DL1 discussion.

Quinnen Williams was back at it in Week 9, tallying three solos, four assists, three tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Now up to five sacks on the season, Williams has been on fire for IDP managers, recording three spike weeks and one splash week in his last four games. Tap Quinnen as a DT1/DL2 option for a plus Week 10 matchup against the struggling Los Angeles Chargers.

Sheldon Rankins stepped up in Week 9, tallying three solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Rankins is up to four sacks on the season, and his big game puts him back on the DT1 map. Start him where needed.

Patrick Jones stepped up in Week 9, notching four solos, two assists, one sack, and three tackles for loss. The sack was the first of the season for Jones, who remains more DL5 than DL4 until Week 11 when six teams are on bye. Look elsewhere for Week 10.

DeMarcus Lawrence stepped up in Week 9, posting two solos, one assist, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. It was the first sack of the season for the Seahawks edge rusher, who saw a season high in snaps (74%) with Leonard Williams sidelined. Continue to treat Lawrence as a low floor DL3/4, regardless of whether or not Williams returns for Week 10.

Josh Uche was back at it in Week 9, recording four solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Uche has just three sacks on the season, but with a sack in back-to-back games, he is now an intriguing DL3 option, especially during the byes. Treat him as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Rashan Gary was excellent in Week 9, racking up five solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Rashan has just two sacks on the season, but still makes for a DL3/4 type at best. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 10 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Cam Heyward showed up in Week 8, reeling off three solos, three assists, 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Heyward is up to 2.5 sacks on the season and remains an elite DT2 play for IDP. He still has a place as a DL3 during the bye weeks, but he has been there for the first seven weeks based more on name equity than actual production. The 1.5 sacks help change that and keep him locked in as a top-36 option for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jacob Martin went berserk in Week 8, tallying four solos, three sacks, and three tackles for loss. Martin clawed his way up to 6.5 sacks in seven games, with five of them coming in three of his last four games. Appearing in this column for the second straight week despite just coming off a bye, Martin's rostership numbers didn't move an inch, theoretically because IDP managers didn't want to burn a spot on him just to have him go on bye. Whatever the case, Martin needs to be treated as a DL2 option while he is hot and may find a new home by the end of the day (Tuesday). Tap Martin as a top-25 option until he starts to cool down.

Byron Murphy stepped up in Week 9, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Murphy is not up to an impressive four sacks and is squarely back in the DT1 mix going forward. Treat him as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Chris Jones showed up in Week 9, racking up two solos, two assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. The sacks were the first full sacks of the season for Jones, who has just 2.5 sacks on the year. The sacks put the Chiefs defensive tackle back on the DT1 map and make him more than a bench clogger in DL leagues. Tap Jones as a DT1/DL4 for a tasty Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

DJ Wonnum is expected to clear concussion protocol in time to suit up for Week 10. If he flies to Munich, he should be considered a lock for the Sunday morning matchup against the New England Patriots. Tap Wonnum as a DL3 option if he is active, as expected.

Clowney is set to get the start for Week 10 with Danielle Hunter ruled out. Up to 3.5 sacks on the season after getting to the quarterback last week, Jadeveon can be counted as a top-36 option for the plus Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Derrick Moore went off in Week 9, tallying two solos, one assist, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. The sacks were the first of the season for the rookie edge rusher, who saw a season high 71 percent of the snaps due to DJ Wonnum being sidelined. Wonnum was fantastic prior to the Lions' Week 6 bye, but Moore should have earned an expanded role with his performance. He will be hard to trust outside the bye weeks until it is confirmed he is getting 50 percent or more of the snaps, but he makes for a solid DL4/flex2 type for the next couple of weeks at the very minimum.

Ashton Gillotte stepped up in Week 9, notching two solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. The sack was the second of the season for Gillotte, who remains someone to leave on wires in 12-team leagues. Look elsewhere for Week 10 outside of 32-team leagues.

LaCale London showed up in Week 9, tallying four solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. It was the second sack of the season for London, who remains more of an option in leagues with 20+ teams than someone who should be on the radar for those in 12-team formats. Look elsewhere for Week 10.

Karl Brooks stepped up in Week 9, notching two solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. The sacks were the first of the season for Brooks, who is now on the DT3 radar. Keep him rostered in deeper DT leagues but look elsewhere in DL leagues.

Caden Curry was back at it in Week 9, reeling off one solo, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. Curry has back-to-back spike weeks and has found himself joining the DL3 conversation. Fire the Colts edge rusher up as an upside DL3 option for a tasty Week 10 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Khristian Boyd showed up in Week 9, tallying three solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. It was the second sack of the season for Boyd, who remains more DT3/4 than DT2. Look elsewhere for Week 10, even in DT leagues.
